opportunities.title: Small-business catalog and spreadsheet cleanup
opportunities.thesis: Small merchants have recurring catalog/data-maintenance work that is too small for agencies but valuable enough to buy as a fixed-price local service.
execution_steps: Interview five merchants and collect examples of recurring catalog or spreadsheet pain.
Offer one narrow fixed-price cleanup package with before/after deliverables.
Complete two paid pilots and measure hours, revisions, acquisition cost, and repeat demand.
Productize the repeatable steps into templates or automation only after paid demand is observed.
failure_modes: Merchant pain exists but willingness to pay is below the estimated range.
Work becomes bespoke and destroys hourly economics.
Customer acquisition takes longer than delivery.

evidence.claim: Synthetic merchant interview batch reports recurring catalog and spreadsheet maintenance pain.
Synthetic paid-pilot ledger supports the declared fixed-price revenue and delivery-cost range.
Synthetic directory sample shows few providers advertising small fixed-price catalog cleanup locally.

opportunities.title: Bilingual storefront and menu conversion
opportunities.thesis: A language-and-digitization skill gap may let a local operator convert offline storefront information into bilingual digital listings and menus.
execution_steps: Verify local business-listing, translation, tax, and invoicing requirements.
Collect ten storefront samples where bilingual information is absent or poor.
Pre-sell a bounded one-page/menu conversion package before automating delivery.
failure_modes: Local merchants do not value bilingual conversion enough to pay.
Platform or local rules require registration not yet modeled.
Translation QA cost removes the price edge.

evidence.claim: Synthetic storefront sample contains businesses with incomplete bilingual information.
Synthetic quote sample suggests a plausible service price range but has not been validated by paid pilots.

opportunities.title: Used-appliance collection and resale route
opportunities.thesis: A local acquisition/resale price spread may exist for working used appliances if transport, storage, inspection, and return costs remain bounded.
execution_steps: Verify resale, waste-handling, transport, warranty, and tax obligations.
Measure acquisition-to-sale spread on a tiny sample before holding inventory.
Model storage, failed units, returns, transport, and time-to-sale as explicit costs.
failure_modes: Capital is trapped in slow inventory.
Transport and defective-unit costs consume the apparent spread.
Permit or waste-handling obligations change the economics.

evidence.claim: Synthetic marketplace sample shows recurring buyer interest in low-cost working appliances.
Synthetic transaction sample exhibits a positive gross acquisition-resale spread before logistics and failure losses.
Synthetic disposal-channel sample indicates recurring potential supply.
Synthetic rules register marks the activity as requiring local resale/waste-handling review before execution.
